_README: Book-wide source register for AI Operations Management.
One entry per source, keyed. Chapters cite by key; footnotes and chapter
source registers are both generated from this file, so a source cited in
two chapters cannot appear two different ways.
Add entries with: python3 sources.py add
Capture with:     python3 sources.py capture
Check status:     python3 sources.py check
Resolve chapters: python3 sources.py build AIOM_ch01.html
FIELDS
type       article | blog | web | social | report
authors    [{family, given}] or [{org}]
title      title of the piece
container  journal, blog, or site name; omit for report
date       ISO. Use YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM, or YYYY
url        canonical URL, after any source upgrade
volume/issue/pages/doi   articles only
perishable true if the page can change or vanish. Drives G1.
wayback    archive link. Filled by: sources.py capture
local      local dark-archive filename. Filled by: sources.py capture
accessed   ISO date of actual capture, not of verification
upgrade    note on a more durable form to chase, or null when settled

altman-2025-pro.title: Post on X on ChatGPT Pro subscription economics
altman-2025-pro.note: Posted 2025-01-05 19:11 US Pacific, which is 2025-01-06 03:11 UTC. X displays 'January 6, 2025' to viewers outside the Americas. The book dates it January 5, 2025, matching US time and TechCrunch's same-day 'on Sunday' report. Flag for fact check so the UTC display is not read as an error. Second path: techcrunch-2025-altman-pro.

anthropic-2025-limits.title: post on X announcing new weekly rate limits for Claude Pro and Max
anthropic-2025-limits.note: Announced 2025-07-28 by email to subscribers and by this post; effective 2025-08-28. The X post is the canonical public form. The chapter's clause about limits introduced quietly earlier in July rests on techcrunch-2025-anthropic-limits, not on this post.

github-2025-premium.title: Update to GitHub Copilot Consumptive Billing Experience
github-2025-premium.note: Upgrade RESOLVED differently from the worksheet. The worksheet called for a permalinked docs.github.com revision. A dated changelog entry is the better artifact for a dated claim: a docs page describes the current state, a changelog records the change on the day it happened. This also matches the chapter's own footnote wording, 'premium-request billing changelog'.

github-2026-usage.title: GitHub Copilot Is Moving to Usage-Based Billing
github-2026-usage.note: Announced 2026-04-27, effective 2026-06-01. Confirms the chapter's claim: premium request units replaced by GitHub AI Credits consumed on token usage, including input, output, and cached tokens, at each model's published API rate. No repo revision exists for this one; it is a github.blog post, not a docs page.

microsoft-2026-q2.title: FY26 Second Quarter Earnings Call
microsoft-2026-q2.note: DECISION 46 (2026-07-28): Microsoft's own IR transcript is accepted as the primary source. The figure is a first-party disclosure by the party that holds the data, published by that party. A filing upgrade is not available: the 4.7 million figure appears only in spoken remarks, the FY26 Q2 press release carries no Copilot subscriber count, and Microsoft does not break out product-level subscriber counts in the 10-Q. Perishable, so capture governs durability. Verified wording, Nadella: 'all up now we have over 4.7 million paid Copilot subscribers, up 75% year-over-year', stated in the coding paragraph, so GitHub Copilot. FLAG FOR FACT CHECK: he said 'over 4.7 million'; the chapter says 'reported at 4.7 million', which understates. Quarter ended 2025-12-31, four months before the 2026-06-01 billing transition the chapter attaches it to.
